newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA expects rate cut by year end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA expects rate cut by year end.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australian (CBA) said on Tuesday that it expects interest rates to fall by the end of the year.
"My feeling is that it is likely to be an easing rather than a tightening in interest rates," CBA chairman Tim Besley told reporters after the bank's annual meeting in Melbourne.
Asked when he expected an interest rate change Besley replied: "before Christmas".
CBA managing director David Murray agreed with the banks chairman over the future direction of interest rates.
"If you look at the bank bill rates now there are already 25 basis points or more factored into the market rate, so it would be possible to change," Murray told reporters after the annual meeting.
Murray said the Reserve Bank of Australia is likely to wait until after September quarter inflation data, due October 23, before they would announce any change in interest rates.
"There is some scope for change at the moment it is just a question of time before the Reserve bank looks at future numbers," Murray said.
The Reserve Bank cut official cash rates by 50 basis points to 7.00 percent on July 31.
